The best molecular substrate is conditional Ser-tRNA-channel fidelity, not ordinary tRNA supply. UCN and AGY are decoded through different Ser-tRNA routes. Under ordinary rich growth, the two routes may be effectively equivalent. Under serine limitation, one-carbon stress, oxidative stress, proteostasis pressure, altered SerRS behavior, or tRNA-modification stress, the degeneracy could be lifted: one island may remain accurate while the other acquires a different near-cognate or mischarging profile. There is empirical precedent that environmental perturbation can split synonymous codons into robust and sensitive classes in E. coli reporters; that study included Ser among the tested codon families, found especially strong splitting in sixfold families, and reported that the hierarchy was not explained by ordinary codon usage or tRNA abundance, but by isoacceptor aminoacylation competition. arXiv But that precedent is also a warning. If the Ser signal is merely “one island has more charged tRNA,” then it fails the question’s constraint. The surviving version must be narrower and stronger: at matched charged-tRNA availability, matched wobble class controls, matched GC, matched codon-pair context, matched mRNA stability, and matched ribosome dwell, UCN and AGY still produce different peptide-resolved error spectra or different wrong-product costs. The decisive confounders are severe. First, tRNA supply in disguise. Any effect predicted by tRNA gene copy, tAI, total Ser-tRNA abundance, or charged Ser-tRNA abundance is not the mechanism. The key signal must be fidelity or wrong-product identity, not substrate availability. Second, wobble in disguise. Since UCN and AGY necessarily use different decoding routes, anticodon position-34 pairing and wobble modifications can easily fake an island effect. A credible residual mechanism must survive after wobble breadth and anticodon modification are removed or controlled. Third, ribosome dwell masquerading as fidelity. Lower reporter output, ribosome pausing, queuing, or drop-off is not enough. The decisive readout is not fluorescence and not ribosome profiling; it is peptide-resolved mistranslation: which wrong amino acids appear at the Ser site, at what rate, under which condition. Fourth, sequence-composition confounding. UCN and AGY differ in GC, purine/pyrimidine pattern, CpG/UpA potential, local motifs, and folding tendencies. Any natural-genome enrichment of one island is weak evidence unless these are neutralized. Fifth, Stop leakage. UCA and UCG have one-step Stop-neighbor risks that UCU/UCC do not. If the observed effect is only UCA/UCG avoidance, then the mechanism is Stop-adjacency, not a sense-side Ser-island mechanism. The surviving signal must distinguish UCN-versus-AGY as islands, not just UCA/UCG-versus-everything. Sixth, protein-position confounding. Ser codon choice may correlate with phosphorylation motifs, disorder, low-complexity sequence, catalytic Ser residues, secretion signals, splice enhancers, or gene class. Those can be real biological patterns without being translation-level codon selection. The same Ser site must change its measured error spectrum or error cost when recoded between UCN and AGY. The weak assumption to challenge is that a missing synonymous Hamming edge is automatically biologically meaningful. It is not. If most relevant errors are third-position wobble errors, the missing bridge between UCN and AGY is nearly irrelevant because both islands already contain internal third-position synonymous protection. The graph defect becomes biologically sharp only if first- or second-position near-cognate errors, mischarging, or proofreading failures contribute enough to make the two Ser islands have different damaging-error spectra. So the strongest answer is not “Ser has two codon families and cells like one better.” It is: cells may use UCN and AGY as two synonymous fidelity modes, choosing the island whose rare mistranslation products are least damaging at highly expressed or functionally constrained Ser sites. The sharpest next question is: At matched Ser sites and matched expression context, does UCN↔AGY recoding change the peptide-resolved mistranslation spectrum in the direction predicted by the natural codon choice at highly expressed, functionally constrained Ser residues?
